caption: What if you lived in the coldest village on Earth? Meet Oymyakon in Siberia, home to about 500 people. In January the average temperature is around -46 °C, while your deep freezer sits at about -18 °C. The official record is -67.7 °C, set in 1933. At that cold, eyelashes freeze, glasses stick to faces and pen ink stops flowing. Cars are kept running all day or parked in heated garages, because a switched-off engine may not start again. The ground is permafrost, so there are no farms: people eat meat and fish, including raw frozen fish shaved into thin curls. School only closes when it drops below roughly -50 °C. India has its own freezer too: Dras in Ladakh reportedly hit about -60 °C in 1995. Plot twist: Oymyakon once reached +34.6 °C in summer, a swing of more than 100 degrees between its records. Could YOU survive a winter there? 👇
